job.title: Rendering Plant Operator
job.description:

Shift Times Rotating roster across:

  • 1:30pm - 9:30pm
  • 9:30pm - 5:30am
Weekend work and additional shifts may be required depending on production requirements.
Key Responsibilities
  • Operate and monitor rendering plant equipment including grinders, cookers, decanters, separators, presses and dryers
  • Receive, load and process raw materials through the rendering operation
  • Monitor cooking temperatures, production flow and operating parameters
  • Complete production, quality and temperature records accurately
  • Inspect finished tallow and identify any quality issues
  • Follow HACCP, food safety and traceability requirements
  • Perform cleaning, sanitation and basic operational maintenance tasks
  • Report equipment faults and production issues promptly

  • Previous experience in manufacturing, food processing, rendering, production or industrial operations

  • Commitment to workplace safety and food quality standards
  • Forklift licence highly regarded but not essential
Apply Now If you're an experienced production operator looking for a stable role within a large industrial processing environment, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today with your current resume.

Looking for a career that offers variety, stability and the chance to work in one of New Zealand's most sought-after locations? Join a leading infrastructure provider delivering essential electricity network services across the Queenstown region.

As a Line Mechanic / Streetlight Electrician, you'll be responsible for installing, maintaining and repairing overhead and underground electricity network infrastructure throughout the Queenstown region.
Working across planned maintenance, upgrades, new installations and fault response activities, you'll play a key role in keeping local communities connected and ensuring the reliability of critical network assets.

  • Accurately complete safety documentation, job sheets and timesheets
  • Maintain high standards of health, safety and environmental compliance

Skills & Experience  

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
  • NZ Registered Line Mechanic qualification or Streetlight Level Standard qualification
  • Current EWRB registration or equivalent recognised assessment
  • Experience working within electricity distribution or network infrastructure environments
  • Full Class 1 Driver Licence
  • Strong commitment to workplace health and safety
  • Ability to work independently and manage time effectively
  • Flexibility to travel and work away from home when required
  • Strong attention to detail and a practical problem-solving approach

Culture
You'll be joining a team that values safety, teamwork and continuous improvement. Employees are empowered to take ownership of their work, support one another and continually develop their skills through structured training and development opportunities.

Our client is a leading infrastructure services provider delivering essential electricity, transport and utility services across New Zealand. You'll be joining crews that take pride in doing the job right the first time. Supervisors are hands-on, communication is straightforward, and quality workmanship is recognised and respected.

job.title: Senior Underground Mine Geologist
job.description:
This is a genuine senior operational geology role with a growing underground gold producer. You'll be a key technical leader on site, working closely with mining, technical services and processing teams to ensure geological information is translated into safe, practical and profitable mining outcomes.

This isn't a role where you'll spend your day behind a computer. We're looking for someone who is technically strong, commercially minded and comfortable being visible underground, supporting production and mentoring a team of geologists.

Why Join?
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a successful underground gold operation.
  • Lead and mentor a team of geologists and contractors.
  • Influence grade control, mine planning and operational performance.
  • Growing multi-site gold producer with strong career progression opportunities.
  • Play a key role in shaping the future of the operation.
Key Responsibilities
  • Provide geological leadership across active underground production areas.
  • Drive excellence in grade control, reconciliation and ore forecasting.
  • Deliver practical geological advice to maximise ore recovery and minimise dilution.
  • Review stoping outcomes and validate grade control performance.
  • Manage geological data collection, validation and interpretation.
  • Track ore movement from underground through to the processing plant.
  • Lead reconciliation activities and identify opportunities for operational improvement.
  • Support mine planning and Life of Mine (LOM) planning activities.
  • Oversee resource and extensional drilling programs.
  • Contribute to safety, risk management and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Mentor, develop and manage geology personnel and contractors.
About You
  • Degree qualified in Geology or related discipline.
  • Strong underground gold mining experience.
  • Experience with grade control, geological modelling and reconciliation.
  • Proficient with Leapfrog and other 3D geological software.
  • Strong understanding of mine-to-mill processes.
  • Demonstrated leadership capability and experience mentoring others.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Resource estimation experience would be highly regarded.
  • Current C Class Manual Driver's Licence.
What's on Offer
  • Competitive salary package.
  • Performance-based bonus scheme.
  • Health and wellness allowance.
  • Health insurance discounts.
  • Salary continuance insurance.
  • 5 years pro-rata long service leave.

What good looks like here

You don't need to know everything on day one. What matters is that you show up, listen, ask questions, work hard and improve every day.

We're looking for someone who wants more than just a pay cheque. Someone who sees this as an opportunity to learn a trade, build valuable skills and create a future for themselves in civil construction.

job.title: National Sales Manager - Line Materials
job.description:
About TEN Group
TEN Group is an established provider of specialised products, technical solutions and services to Australia’s electricity transmission and distribution sectors.

Working closely with utilities, asset owners, engineering teams and major contractors, TEN Group supports the construction, operation and maintenance of critical electricity-network infrastructure.

Stellar Recruitment is partnering with TEN Group to appoint a National Sales Manager to lead its Line Materials division.

About the role
Reporting to the General Manager Sales & Marketing, this newly created, customer-facing position will own the division’s strategic relationships, opportunity pipeline, sales budget, gross margin, contract portfolio and customer outcomes.

The business has a strong foundation across major transmission projects, utility maintenance programs and recurring supply contracts. The opportunity is to build a visible national presence with customers, identify and qualify opportunities earlier, shape specifications and commercial strategies, and convert project activity, tenders and approvals into profitable contracted demand.

You will provide commercial leadership to an experienced team and oversee the internal disciplines supporting tenders and contract management, coordinating closely with engineering, technical sales, product quality, testing, Finance, Legal, Supply Chain and Operations. The technical capability is already established, your focus will combine customer engagement with strong commercial governance, disciplined execution, risk management and accountability for growth.

Key responsibilities
  • Develop and execute the national Line Materials sales and customer strategy.
  • Maintain a strong national market presence through regular engagement with utilities, asset owners, engineers and major contractors.
  • Build strategic account plans and deepen relationships with key customers and industry stakeholders.
  • Proactively identify, create and qualify opportunities across transmission, distribution and utility-maintenance markets.
  • Own a disciplined, stage-based pipeline from early customer engagement and specification through tender, negotiation, award and delivery handover.
  • Drive opportunity conversion, forecasting accuracy and clear next-step accountability across the team.
  • Oversee the divisional tender function and lead bid execution, including opportunity prioritisation, bid strategy, pricing, supply assumptions, governance, approvals, negotiation, contract risk and margin protection.
  • Oversee contract management across the portfolio, ensuring disciplined mobilisation, administration of obligations and variations, renewals, price reviews, product additions, risk controls and performance improvement.
  • Own revenue, gross margin, expenditure and performance against budget.
  • Lead the commercial prioritisation of utility approvals, trials and engineering specifications.
  • Monitor contractual performance, including DIFOT, lead times, quality and other customer KPIs, and lead corrective commercial actions where required.
  • Use CRM, reporting and pipeline reviews to strengthen visibility, decision-making and accountability.
  • Establish clear internal commercial rhythms, controls and accountabilities across Product Management, Supply Chain, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Service to deliver customer and commercial outcomes.
  • Coach and develop the team while building a proactive, customer-focused sales culture.
The position will act as the commercial owner of divisional outcomes, overseeing tender and contract-management processes and coordinating the relevant specialists, while technical sign-off, legal advice and operational delivery remain with those functions.

About you
You will be an experienced, customer-facing B2B sales and commercial leader with a record of developing strategic accounts, generating and converting complex opportunities, overseeing tender and contract-management functions, and delivering profitable growth in electricity networks, utilities, transmission infrastructure, line materials or a closely related technical market.

You understand that major utility and infrastructure opportunities are won through sustained relationships, technical credibility, early stakeholder engagement, disciplined tender execution and strong commercial management.

You will ideally bring:
  • Substantial customer-facing sales leadership experience in a technical B2B environment.
  • Strong exposure to utilities, transmission, distribution or electrical infrastructure.
  • A demonstrated record of strategic account development, pipeline generation and opportunity conversion.
  • Ownership of a sales budget, gross margin, commercial controls and complex contract portfolio.
  • Demonstrated experience managing or overseeing a tender function, including bid strategy, governance, pricing, approvals, negotiation and long-cycle infrastructure submissions.
  • Demonstrated experience managing or overseeing complex contract portfolios, including mobilisation, obligations, variations, renewals, commercial risk and customer performance.
  • Experience leading technical sales or engineering-focused teams.
  • Established relationships with utilities, asset owners or major contractors.
  • Sound judgement across pricing, contract risk, forecasting and customer commitments.
  • Strong CRM, pipeline-management and analytical capability.
  • A calm, credible and collaborative leadership style.
  • Experience with utility product approvals, engineering specifications, testing, standards-driven procurement or annuity contracts would be highly regarded.
  • Direct line-materials experience is advantageous but not essential. TEN Group is open to candidates from adjacent electrical, utility or engineered-infrastructure markets with the required commercial leadership and sector credibility.
Why join TEN Group?
  • Own the profitable growth of a strategically important national division.
  • Build influential relationships across Australia’s utility and infrastructure markets.
  • Lead a high-value portfolio of major projects, tenders and contracts.
  • Work directly with the General Manager Sales & Marketing.
  • Partner with an experienced team with considerable technical knowledge.
  • Shape customer strategy, commercial systems, market engagement and future growth.
  • Join a collaborative culture built around accountability, customer outcomes and continuous improvement.
This is an opportunity to become the customer-facing commercial leader of an established technical division, shape national market relationships and convert a strong opportunity base into sustainable, profitable growth.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Stellar Recruitment or submit your application through the link provided.

Harmony is the largest gold producer by volume in South Africa and is a significant operator of gold tailings retreatment facilities. In Australia, Harmony owns the high-grade CSA copper mine in Cobar, NSW and is constructing the Eva Copper Mine in Cloncurry, QLD. These assets are supported by the Harmony Australasia regional corporate office located in Milton, Brisbane.
  
The Eva Copper Mine is a significant and strategically important project for Harmony marking a major milestone in the company’s copper growth strategy and its long-term commitment to Northwest Queensland. The mine will have a minimum life of 15 years and will involve mining multiple open cut pits providing copper bearing ore to a concentrator. Role 1 - This is a site-based role supervising a heavy civils and bulk earthworks scope constructing a major tailings storage facility (TSF) across a major program of works. You will work closely with contractors and project teams to ensure construction, safety, quality, program and environmental requirements are met on site.

Role 1 - This is a site-based role supervising a broad scope to include SMP, structural steel and concrete packages across a major program of works. You will work closely with contractors and project teams to ensure construction, safety, quality, program and environmental requirements are met on site.

  • Acting as the key point of contact for contractors and the owner’s team on technical issues and site queries.

  • Liaising and supporting project teams to support efficient delivery and maintaining program.
This role suits a hands-on Supervisor who thrives in a site environment and enjoys turning plans into safe, high-quality outcomes.
  
This role will be DIDO from local communities or FIFO from Brisbane or Townsville to our site in Cloncurry NW QLD, with local candidates highly regarded. Local employees are paid a regional allowance and a competitive salary. Roster is 14 days on, 7 days off.
  
Please note: this is a maximum term role aligned with the project completion and close out.

job.title: Shipping Officer
job.description:
• Growth and development-focused employer
  • Work alongside a collaborative, high-performing team
  • Stunning Newcastle CBD office and free parking
About the Client:

MACH Energy operates a modern, low-cost coal mining operation in the Hunter Valley, benefiting from a low strip ratio and an efficient fleet of excavators, trucks, and other essential mining equipment. They are continuously expanding their operations year in, year out, supported by significant infrastructure investments and strategic growth plans.
  
Based in the heart of Newcastle's CBD, MACH Energy’s newly appointed corporate office offers breathtaking views of the harbour. They have state-of-the-art facilities, including video conferencing, end-of-trip facilities, a large kitchen, and an array of employee meeting and break-out spaces – plus parking!

About the Role:

Reporting to the Senior Contract & Shipping Officer, the Shipping Officer is responsible for preparing and coordinating the shipping, customs and cargo documentation required for the export of coal, and supporting the coordination of vessel loading, laytime and demurrage processes. As the primary point of liaison with the vessel, the vessel’s Master and the vessel’s agent throughout the shipping cycle, you’ll play a key role in keeping MACH Energy’s coal shipments moving smoothly and compliantly out of the Port of Newcastle.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Preparing and issuing Shipper’s Declarations for each shipment parcel and submitting them to AMSA and the vessel’s agent
  • Drafting pre-shipment cargo documentation, including Bills of Lading, Statements of Fact, Cargo Manifests, Stowage Plans, Proforma Invoices and Certificates of Origin, in line with Letters of Credit and shipping instructions
  • Raising Export Declaration Numbers (EDNs) and preparing pre-arrival documentation for vessel agents
  • Reviewing, accepting and returning Notices of Readiness in accordance with contract requirements
  • Preparing shipment fixture nominations for the Superintendent Company and coordinating with the Marine Surveyor
  • Finalising documentation for the Master’s review and signing, and coordinating the release, endorsement and courier dispatch of Original Bills of Lading and cargo documents
  • Providing timely shipment updates to customers, including port times, draught survey results and final Bills of Lading
  • Preparing laytime calculations, resolving routine laytime queries with customers, and working with the Accounts team on demurrage debit notes and despatch invoices
  • Maintaining accurate export documentation status tracking and vessel records for all shipments
To be successful in this role you will have:
  • 3–5 years’ experience in bulk shipping, port logistics or maritime operations, specifically dealing with bulk commodities
  • A tertiary qualification in Business, International Trade, Logistics or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience preparing and managing export shipping and customs documentation, including Bills of Lading, Cargo Manifests, Statements of Fact, Stowage Plans, Shipper’s Declarations, Certificates of Origin and EDNs
  • Experience preparing and negotiating laytime calculations, with sound commercial awareness of demurrage exposure and dispute prevention
  • Experience liaising directly with vessel agents, vessel Masters and internal stakeholders (including Accounts) throughout the shipping and laytime cycle
  • General exposure to vessel berthing, loading and sailing coordination in a port environment
  • Experience using the Australian Government Department of Home Affairs Cargo Interactive system
  • Working knowledge of Incoterms (e.g. FOB, CFR, CIF)
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook)
  • A high level of accuracy and attention to detail when preparing statutory, customs and commercial shipping documentation
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills, and the ability to stay organised and meet deadlines under high-pressure, time-sensitive conditions
  • A current Australian driver’s licence
What’s on Offer:
  • Attractive salary and benefits package tailored to your experience and skills
  • Join a company that values a One Team culture
  • Ongoing professional development to support your growth
  • State-of-the-art facilities in the Newcastle CBD, with parking
  • Access to MACH Energy’s Healthy Lifestyle Program
Next Steps:

Please apply via SEEK or LinkedIn and a representative from Stellar Recruitment will be in touch to discuss your application and walk you through next steps.

job.title: Shipping Officer
job.description:
• Growth and development-focused employer
  • Work alongside a collaborative, high-performing team
  • Stunning Newcastle CBD office and free parking
About the Client:

MACH Energy operates a modern, low-cost coal mining operation in the Hunter Valley, benefiting from a low strip ratio and an efficient fleet of excavators, trucks, and other essential mining equipment. They are continuously expanding their operations year in, year out, supported by significant infrastructure investments and strategic growth plans.
  
Based in the heart of Newcastle's CBD, MACH Energy’s newly appointed corporate office offers breathtaking views of the harbour. They have state-of-the-art facilities, including video conferencing, end-of-trip facilities, a large kitchen, and an array of employee meeting and break-out spaces – plus parking!

About the Role:

Reporting to the Senior Contract & Shipping Officer, the Shipping Officer is responsible for preparing and coordinating the shipping, customs and cargo documentation required for the export of coal, and supporting the coordination of vessel loading, laytime and demurrage processes. As the primary point of liaison with the vessel, the vessel’s Master and the vessel’s agent throughout the shipping cycle, you’ll play a key role in keeping MACH Energy’s coal shipments moving smoothly and compliantly out of the Port of Newcastle.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Preparing and issuing Shipper’s Declarations for each shipment parcel and submitting them to AMSA and the vessel’s agent
  • Drafting pre-shipment cargo documentation, including Bills of Lading, Statements of Fact, Cargo Manifests, Stowage Plans, Proforma Invoices and Certificates of Origin, in line with Letters of Credit and shipping instructions
  • Raising Export Declaration Numbers (EDNs) and preparing pre-arrival documentation for vessel agents
  • Reviewing, accepting and returning Notices of Readiness in accordance with contract requirements
  • Preparing shipment fixture nominations for the Superintendent Company and coordinating with the Marine Surveyor
  • Finalising documentation for the Master’s review and signing, and coordinating the release, endorsement and courier dispatch of Original Bills of Lading and cargo documents
  • Providing timely shipment updates to customers, including port times, draught survey results and final Bills of Lading
  • Preparing laytime calculations, resolving routine laytime queries with customers, and working with the Accounts team on demurrage debit notes and despatch invoices
  • Maintaining accurate export documentation status tracking and vessel records for all shipments
To be successful in this role you will have:
  • 3–5 years’ experience in bulk shipping, port logistics or maritime operations, specifically dealing with bulk commodities
  • A tertiary qualification in Business, International Trade, Logistics or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience preparing and managing export shipping and customs documentation, including Bills of Lading, Cargo Manifests, Statements of Fact, Stowage Plans, Shipper’s Declarations, Certificates of Origin and EDNs
  • Experience preparing and negotiating laytime calculations, with sound commercial awareness of demurrage exposure and dispute prevention
  • Experience liaising directly with vessel agents, vessel Masters and internal stakeholders (including Accounts) throughout the shipping and laytime cycle
  • General exposure to vessel berthing, loading and sailing coordination in a port environment
  • Experience using the Australian Government Department of Home Affairs Cargo Interactive system
  • Working knowledge of Incoterms (e.g. FOB, CFR, CIF)
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook)
  • A high level of accuracy and attention to detail when preparing statutory, customs and commercial shipping documentation
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills, and the ability to stay organised and meet deadlines under high-pressure, time-sensitive conditions
  • A current Australian driver’s licence
What’s on Offer:
  • Attractive salary and benefits package tailored to your experience and skills
  • Join a company that values a One Team culture
  • Ongoing professional development to support your growth
  • State-of-the-art facilities in the Newcastle CBD, with parking
  • Access to MACH Energy’s Healthy Lifestyle Program
Next Steps:

Please apply via SEEK or LinkedIn and a representative from Stellar Recruitment will be in touch to discuss your application and walk you through next steps.

job.title: Sales & Events Manager
job.description:
Sales and Event Manager
 
Aka Rooftop is an Asian kitchen and bar above Auckland city, hosting corporate functions, private celebrations, brand launches and venue events.
 
Role purpose
Grow profitable bookings for Aka Rooftop by finding customers, developing relationships and converting enquiries into confirmed corporate functions, private celebrations and venue events. The role owns the sales process from first contact through to booking confirmation and a clear handover to the events and operations team.
 
Core responsibilities
  • Win new business through targeted outreach to corporate clients, event planners and relevant partners, and build repeat business through active account management and follow-up.
  • Qualify enquiries, lead venue tours and prepare tailored proposals. Follow up consistently, negotiate within agreed pricing and delegated authority, and close bookings.
  • Maintain an accurate CRM and a qualified sales pipeline, recording client needs, value, stage, next action and expected decision date. Report progress and forecast bookings weekly.
  • Protect commercial value by using approved packages and pricing, checking capacity with operations, and seeking approval for discounts or non-standard terms.
  • Work with accounts on deposits and payment milestones. Document agreed event requirements and hand confirmed bookings to the events and operations teams.
  • Work with the Marketing Manager to identify target audiences, improve enquiry quality and track which activity produces confirmed bookings.
  • Follow Aka Rooftop health and safety and host responsibility requirements when running tours and events.
Capabilities and experience
  • At least 3 years of relevant sales experience, ideally 5 years, with demonstrated success winning and converting business. Venue, hotel, hospitality or event sales experience is desirable. You can explain your personal contribution and measurable results.
  • Confidence in prospecting, client meetings, venue tours, proposals and negotiation, with strong judgement about client fit, value and follow-up priorities.
  • Accurate CRM use, pipeline management and forecasting, and the ability to act on conversion data and lost-booking reasons.
  • Clear communication and reliable coordination with marketing, accounts, food and beverage, and event delivery colleagues.
  • Sound understanding of event requirements and hospitality service, balancing client expectations, venue capacity and profitability.
  • Right to work in New Zealand.
Role boundaries and working relationships
  • Sales is the main priority. The Marketing Manager owns marketing, brand and campaigns; this role owns sales conversations, proposals, relationship development and booking conversion, and works with marketing to improve lead generation.
  • The Events Coordinator and operations team support event delivery and logistics. This role provides a complete handover and resolves sales-related client questions; delivery responsibilities are agreed with operations.
  • The role does not approve unbudgeted expenditure, exceptional discounts or non-standard commercial terms beyond its delegated authority. Accounts retains its financial controls and payment processing.
First 90 days
  • First 30 days: review enquiries, bookings, repeat accounts, CRM quality and upcoming events; establish baselines for conversion, revenue and margin; agree target clients, sales authority and monthly targets with the owners and operations.
  • By 60 days: run a consistent prospecting and account follow-up routine, maintain a qualified pipeline, report weekly and use a documented booking handover process.
  • By 90 days: review confirmed bookings, profitability, conversion and new and repeat business against the agreed baseline and refine priorities using actual results.
Performance measures
  • Commercial results are the primary measure. The measures below are reviewed with the role holder as part of regular performance conversations. Targets are agreed with the role holder after the first-month baseline review, and the pipeline is reviewed weekly.
 
Measure     -     What is tracked     -    Expectation
    
 Commercial results
     Confirmed booking revenue and event contribution or margin against agreed monthly targets.
     Targets agreed in the first 30 days.
    
 Enquiry conversion
     Eligible enquiries that become confirmed bookings, with lost-booking reasons recorded.
     Baseline set, then improvement target agreed.
    
New and repeat business
     Proactively sourced new accounts and repeat bookings, with source recorded in the CRM.
     Targets agreed after baseline review.
    
Qualified pipeline
     Value and number of viable opportunities by stage, with next action and expected decision date.
     Weekly pipeline and forecast report.
    
Response and sales discipline
     Time to a meaningful first response, completed follow-ups and CRM completeness.
     Aim to respond to enquiries within one business day.
    
Handover quality
     Confirmed bookings with documented requirements, agreed pricing, deposit status and timing.
     Complete handover before each event, by the lead time agreed with operations.

job.description:
SALES & PRODUCT MANAGER – Agriculture Machinery

Are you a commercially minded agricultural machinery professional who knows how to turn product knowledge and market opportunities into sales growth?
Our client is looking for a dynamic Sales & Product Manager – Tractors to lead the sales performance, product portfolio and market development of well-known tractor brands across New Zealand.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the General Manager, you will take ownership of tractor sales performance, product strategy and dealer development. You’ll work with international manufacturers, agricultural dealerships and internal teams to maximise sales opportunities, improve product positioning and grow market share.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who combines strong sales capability with product management expertise and a genuine passion for agricultural machinery.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Sales leadership: Develop and execute sales plans to achieve revenue, gross margin, unit volume and market share targets.
  • Product management: Manage product portfolios, specifications, pricing, positioning and new product introductions.

 Ready to move beyond traditional legal advice and become a true commercial partner to the business? My client is a highly recognised New Zealand organisation that is looking to appoint an experienced Senior Legal Counsel to join its Legal & Compliance function.

job.title: Mining Engineer - Medium Term Planning
job.description:
• Brisbane or site based permanent position
  • Medium term planning for George Fisher Mine
  • Attractive salary and benefits package
The operation:
  
George Fisher Mine (GFM) is a large-scale underground zinc-lead-silver operation based in Mt Isa, QLD. GFM has complex mining sequence, multiple operating fronts, and significant interactions among development, stoping, ventilation, backfill, infrastructure, services, and production readiness.
  
George Fisher has a long mine life and is a key strategic asset for Glencore globally.
  
The role:
  
The Mining Engineer - Medium Term Planning is responsible for developing, maintaining and continuously improving mine plans and schedules that support delivery of production and development targets.
  
Your ability to translate Translate Life-of-Mine and long-term planning strategies into practical medium-term mining sequences that optimise stope extraction, development timing, ventilation availability, and infrastructure readiness and that can be translated into short term plans will be critical.
  
The position can be Brisbane based, FIFO to Mt Isa or Mt Isa based.
  
Experience required:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering or related subject
  • Demonstrated experience in underground hard rock mining, preferably with exposure to mine planning, scheduling or technical services roles.
  • Experience using mine planning and design software (e.g. Deswik, Surpac or equivalent) for development planning, stope sequencing and schedule analysis.
  • Strong understanding of underground mining methods, development requirements and production sequencing.
  • Ability to interpret and integrate geological, geotechnical, ventilation and operational constraints into practical mine plans.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess planning risks, identify constraints and develop practical solutions.
Benefits on offer:
  • Permanent position working directly for Glencore.
  • Competitive salary package including 13% super, generous incentive scheme.
  • Access to training and professional development
  • Opportunity to work for a large mining company with opportunities to advance your career domestically and internationally.
  • Visa sponsorship available for suitability qualified candidates
  • Options for Brisbane based, FIFO to Mt Isa or Mt Isa residential
Next Steps:
  
Glencore has partnered with Stellar Recruitment to manage the recruitment and search for this position. Please contact Lucas Eyers to discuss further or apply direct via email / SEEK.
  
All conversations will be in confidence.

job.title: Practice Lead - Geotechnical
job.description:
• Manager level technical leadership position
  • Work across George Fisher U/G and other growth assets in MT Isa
  • Considerable salary and benefits package - FIFO or Residential
The operation:

George Fisher Mine (GFM) is a large-scale underground zinc-lead-silver operation based in Mt Isa, QLD. George Fisher is one of Australia's most geotechnically challenging underground base-metal mines because it combines a deep, high-stress environment with a large, steeply dipping orebody that is mined using longhole open stoping. The resulting technical challenges would be an attractive challenge to a seasoned geotechnical professional.

George Fisher has a long mine life and is a key strategic asset for Glencore globally. Glencore is also progressing the Blackstar open pit project in Mt Isa. This brownfield expansion is scheduled to move into execution in 2027.

The role:

The Geotechnical Practice Lead works within the Technical Services team to support the Geotechnical Superintendent in delivering safe, practical and value-adding geotechnical outcomes across the operation. The role provides technical leadership across geotechnical monitoring, excavation stability, support design, stope design guideline optimisation, risk management and continuous improvement.

This role is suited to a highly capable geotechnical engineer who combines strong technical depth, strategic thinking, practical operational understanding and a commitment to improving both geotechnical quality and team capability.

Ideally the position would be residentially based in Mt Isa with an attractive package on offer to attract the right person. However, consideration may be given to other arrangements pending your personal circumstances and capability.

Experience required:
  • Tertiary qualification in Geotechnical Engineering or related discipline
  • Significant underground metalliferous mining experience in geotechnical engineering roles.
  • Demonstrated experience in ground control, excavation performance, support design, stope and development geotechnical assessment, and monitoring systems.
  • Strong understanding of underground mining methods and the interaction between geology, stress, excavation geometry, sequencing and support performance.
  • Strong knowledge of geotechnical risk assessment, TARPs, inspections, instrumentation and reconciliation processes.
  • Proven ability to apply geotechnical analysis to practical operational decisions.
  • Experience leading technical teams, mentoring engineers and setting clear standards and expectations.
Benefits on offer:
  • Permanent position working directly for Glencore.
  • Competitive salary package including 13% super and generous incentive scheme.
  • For those considering residential Mt Isa housing and vehicle would be provided - otherwise FIFO is available and we can be flexible on roster
  • Access to training and professional development
  • Opportunity to work for a large mining company with opportunities to advance your career domestically and internationally.
  • Visa sponsorship available for suitability qualified candidates

job.title: Operations Manager- Co-Living
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity to build an accommodation business from the ground up.

Imagine joining a highly successful, privately owned property group at the beginning of an exciting new chapter.

Backed by an accomplished entrepreneur with a proven track record of building successful businesses, this venture will establish a new co-living offering, commencing with a 300-bed development in Melbourne.

With an ambitious expansion strategy already taking shape across Australia's eastern seaboard, this is an opportunity to do considerably more than manage a property.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the founder, you will take ownership of the journey from concept through to a fully operational accommodation business.

Joining during the formative stages, you will influence how the asset is designed, fitted out, marketed and operated, ensuring every decision contributes to an exceptional resident experience and commercially successful business.

  • Working alongside the development team to influence design, fit-out, functionality and operational readiness.
  • Developing the operating model, systems, processes and technology required to launch and manage the facility.
  • Establishing the commercial strategy, including pricing, leasing, marketing and resident acquisition.

  • Overseeing pre-opening preparations, commissioning, mobilisation and the transition into operations.
  • Driving occupancy, revenue, operating performance and resident satisfaction.
  • Creating a scalable operating blueprint to support future developments across the eastern seaboard.
About You

You will bring proven leadership experience from the student accommodation, purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) or co-living sector.

Importantly, you will have previously played a leading role in taking a new accommodation development from concept or pre-opening through to a successful operating business.

Why This Opportunity?

Few roles offer the chance to influence a business so comprehensively from its inception.

You will work directly with a highly experienced and successful entrepreneur who is committed to the venture and prepared to provide the right person with genuine autonomy.

There is an established development opportunity, an ambitious growth strategy and the backing to turn that strategy into reality.

Your influence will extend well beyond the first building. You will help define what this business becomes.

An attractive executive remuneration package and performance incentives will be negotiated commensurate with experience.

job.title: Senior Construction Manager
job.description:
Senior Construction Manager | Data Centres
Major Queensland Data Centre | FIFO / DIDO 
 
The Opportunity
An opportunity has become available for an experienced Senior Project/Construction Manager to take a lead client-side delivery role on a major, high-value data centre development in Queensland.
 
Working with a global project and programme management consultancy, you will be embedded within the client team and act as a senior representative on the ground, providing oversight across the developer, head contractor and wider delivery team.
 
This is not a traditional coordination-focused Project Manager position. You will be expected to understand what is happening on site, challenge programme and contractor performance, identify risks early and ensure the client has clear visibility across delivery.
 
The role is offered on a FIFO/DIDO basis, with flexibility around where you are based for the right candidate.
 
The Role
You will provide senior oversight throughout construction and play a key role in protecting programme, quality and critical milestones.
 
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Representing the client throughout construction delivery
  • Providing oversight across the developer and head contractor
  • Leading regular site reviews and developer meetings
  • Monitoring programme, milestones and critical path
  • Identifying delays, blockers and delivery risks before they impact the client
  • Challenging contractor performance and driving accountability
  • Identifying acceleration and programme recovery opportunities
  • Managing interfaces across GC, electrical and mechanical contractors
  • Monitoring MEP, services and commissioning activities
  • Ensuring works are inspection and milestone ready
  • Providing clear reporting around programme, risk, actions and recovery strategies
  • Maintaining strong relationships across client, developer, contractor and consultant teams
About You
This position requires someone with genuine construction delivery experience who is comfortable operating at a senior level within a complex, fast-moving project environment.
 
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Approximately 10-15+ years' project/construction delivery experience
  • Strong data centre or mission-critical project experience
  • Head Contractor / General Contractor background highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of construction methodology and site delivery
  • Experience across MEP, building services and commissioning
  • Strong programme and critical path management capability
  • Experience identifying and implementing programme recovery strategies
  • Ability to challenge senior contractors and developers constructively
  • Strong commercial and risk awareness
  • Confidence operating as a senior client representative
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in Construction Management, Engineering or similar
Candidates from a consultancy background will also be considered where they can demonstrate strong technical and mission-critical project delivery experience.
 
Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an opportunity to move beyond traditional project coordination and represent the client on one of Queensland's significant emerging data centre developments. You'll be joining a globally recognised consultancy with an established data centre capability and exposure to major projects across Australia and internationally.
 
If you have delivered major data centre, mission-critical or technically complex projects and are looking for an opportunity with genuine client-side influence, I'd be keen to have a confidential conversation.
 
Apply now or contact Monique at Stellar Recruitment for further information.

job.title: Site Safety Supervisor
job.description:
Site Safety Supervisor
Auckland - Fixed-Term Contract
  
Are you an experienced Health & Safety professional who enjoys being in the field, working alongside crews and ensuring critical controls are effective where they matter most?
  
We are seeking a hands-on Site Safety Supervisor to support a major project within an operating fuel terminal. This site-based role focuses on safety leadership, critical risk verification, permit compliance and helping construction teams deliver work safely and efficiently.
  
About the Role
Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for providing day-to-day safety assurance across multiple work fronts, ensuring activities are undertaken in accordance with approved safety plans, permits, procedures and critical risk controls.
  
Key activities will include:
  • Conduct site inspections, audits and verify critical safety controls across active work fronts.
  • Monitor permits, isolations, confined space activities and high-risk work compliance.
  • Oversee lifting operations, scaffolding, work at height and hot work activities.
  • Participate in pre-starts, work planning and provide practical safety guidance to site teams.
  • Investigate incidents and near misses while managing corrective actions and safety reporting.
  • Coordinate with contractors and stakeholders to ensure safe project delivery and emergency readiness.
  
About You
To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
  • NZ Level 4 Health & Safety qualification (or equivalent) with 5+ years' site-based HSE experience.
  • Strong background in high-risk industrial, construction, shutdown or maintenance environments.
  • Proven knowledge of permits, confined spaces, isolations, lifting, work at height and hot work.
  • Current First Aid certification and experience investigating incidents and corrective actions.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills across multiple contractors and workgroups.
  • Confident promoting safe work practices and influencing positive safety behaviours on site.
  
Highly Regarded
  • Diploma-level H&S qualifications, NEBOSH, IOSH or similar
  • ICAM or equivalent investigation training
  • Experience working around tank infrastructure, fuel terminals, refineries, energy facilities or other high-hazard sites
  • Knowledge of occupational hygiene and exposure monitoring programmes
  
What's on Offer?
  • Major industrial project with an immediate start available.
  • High-autonomy role with ownership of site safety outcomes.
  • Work alongside an experienced and collaborative project team.
  • Competitive remuneration package on offer.
  • Fixed-term contract running through to March 2027.
  
If you're a proactive safety professional who enjoys being on site, building relationships with crews and ensuring work is completed safely and efficiently, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Superintendent - Metallurgy
job.description:
• Lead metallurgy, process control and laboratory performance at a major zinc-lead operation
  • Senior leadership role with Glencore’s McArthur River Mine
  • Attractive FIFO roster, competitive remuneration and long-term career opportunities
Stellar Recruitment is partnering with Glencore to appoint a Superintendent – Metallurgy at McArthur River Mine in the Northern Territory.
Located approximately 970 kilometres south-east of Darwin, McArthur River Mine is one of Australia’s largest zinc-lead operations. The site incorporates an open-cut mine, processing facilities and a logistics network transporting concentrate to the Bing Bong Loading Facility for export to customers around the world.

This is an opportunity to take a senior leadership role within a technically complex processing operation and influence plant performance, recovery, product quality and continuous improvement.

The role:

Reporting to the Manager – Metallurgy and Port Operations, the Superintendent – Metallurgy will lead the site’s metallurgical, process-control and laboratory functions.

You will be accountable for ensuring metallurgical systems operate safely and effectively while delivering planned production volumes and product-quality outcomes. The position will provide technical leadership to the metallurgy and laboratory teams and work closely with processing, maintenance, technical and HSE stakeholders.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Monitor and optimise plant metallurgical performance and process-control systems.
  • Identify performance constraints and coordinate practical remedial actions.
  • Lead the implementation of new process systems, equipment and plant upgrades.
  • Drive improvements in recovery, throughput, stability and concentrate quality.
  • Ensure the metallurgical laboratory operates safely, efficiently and in accordance with required standards.
  • Provide technical direction, coaching and development to metallurgical and laboratory personnel.
  • Lead, mentor and manage a multidisciplinary metallurgy and laboratory team.
  • Contribute to annual business plans, operating budgets, capital budgets and performance reporting.
  • Manage the availability, consumption and cost-effective use of major plant consumables.
  • Support plant trials, technical investigations and improvement projects.
  • Work collaboratively with production, maintenance and HSE teams to deliver safe and sustainable operational outcomes.
About You:

To succeed in this position, you will bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Metallurgical, Chemical or Process Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Substantial practical experience within mineral-processing or metallurgical plant operations.
  • Strong knowledge of metallurgical processes, plant optimisation and process-control systems.
  • Experience in complex base-metal concentrators or flotation operations will be highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience managing metallurgists, laboratory personnel or processing technical teams.
  • A sound understanding of metallurgical laboratory practices, sampling, analysis and quality control.
  • Experience delivering process-improvement initiatives, plant trials, equipment upgrades or operational projects.
  • Exposure to operating budgets, capital planning, cost control and technical performance reporting.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and decision-making capability.
  • The ability to translate technical findings into clear operational actions.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across operational and technical functions.
Benefits:
  • Permanent senior leadership opportunity with Glencore.
  • Attractive FIFO 9 days on 5 days off roster from any capital city
  • Competitive remuneration package and applicable site benefits.
  • Support from an experienced site leadership and technical-services team.
  • Long-term professional development opportunities across Glencore’s Australian and international operations.
  • Work within a large-scale operation offering complex technical challenges and significant scope for improvement.

This recruitment process is being managed by Lucas Eyers at Stellar Recruitment. Please apply via SEEK or LinkedIn or contact Lucas directly to discuss in confidence.

job.title: National Engagement Lead
job.description:
About TIACS

We are all about showing up where it matters — on worksites, in communities, and alongside the people and industries we’re in it with.

We are building one of the most innovative social purpose counselling services in the country and are looking for an experienced National Engagement Lead to join the team.

TIACS is Australia’s home of blue-collar counselling, providing free, confidential and accessible professional support to tradies, truckies, farmers, apprentices, blue-collar workers and the people who care about them.

No waitlists. No referrals. No cost.

This role is about making sure the people who need that support know TIACS exists, trust the service, and know how to access it.

TIACS - The Home of Blue Collar Counselling By Industry for Industry

The role

This is not a desk-based role.

Based in Brisbane, you’ll work nationally across worksites, industry events and community initiatives, building trusted relationships with workers, employers, industry groups and decision-makers.

You’ll lead TIACS’ engagement activity across priority industries and regions, while connecting on-the-ground insights with the broader partnerships strategy to identify opportunities and create longer-term impact.

The role includes regular interstate and regional travel, early starts, evening events and occasional weekend work.

If you enjoy being out with people and building relationships face-to-face, this could be a great fit.

What you’ll be doing
  • Building trusted relationships with workers, employers, supervisors and industry leaders
  • Representing TIACS across worksites, industry events and community activities
  • Delivering practical, relatable engagement that makes mental health support easier to understand and access
  • Building repeat engagement across priority industries and regions
  • Identifying partnership, alliance and fundraising opportunities from conversations in the field
  • Working closely with the Head of Partnerships & Impact to progress opportunities
  • Coordinating national engagement activity, bookings and travel
  • Capturing engagement activity, contacts and insights in HubSpot
  • Sharing on-the-ground themes, barriers and opportunities with the wider TIACS team
  • Supporting and guiding the Industry & Community Engagement Officer where required
Who we’re looking for

You do not need to be a counsellor. This is a non-clinical role.

We’re looking for someone grounded, credible and genuinely good with people.
You might come from a community engagement, partnerships, fundraising or field-based background.

More importantly, you’ll be someone who can walk onto a worksite and connect naturally with the crew, then sit down with senior leaders and hold your own.

You’ll need to be able to:
  • Build trust without relying on a polished sales pitch
  • Communicate naturally with different audiences
  • Handle sensitive conversations with good judgement and clear boundaries
  • Work independently and stay organised across a national travel schedule
  • Follow through on conversations and relationships h
  • Represent TIACS in a way that is authentic, approachable and down to earth
How to apply:

Apply via SEEK for a confidential discussion.

Consultant: Bree Purcell | Corporate & Commercial
Email: bree.p@stellarrecruitment.com.au

job.title: Parts Correspondent
job.description:
The role:
If you're organised, customer-focused, and passionate about parts, this is a great opportunity to join TDX as a Parts Correspondent. You'll play an important role in managing customer enquiries, processing orders, providing product information, and ensuring parts solutions are delivered efficiently and accurately.

Reporting to the Parts Manager, you will be responsible for interpreting customer enquiries, processing orders accurately, coordinating parts availability, and supporting internal teams to ensure customers receive the highest level of service.

 Responsibilities include:
  • Provide face-to-face, over the phone and email support and advice to our customers to ensure they receive the right part, at the right price, at the right time and place.
  • Interpret & process incoming purchase orders for efficient dispatch
  • Coordinate the dispatch of customer orders within an acceptable time frame, ensuring all documentation requirements are met
  • Quote enquiries, monitor sales orders daily
  • Be committed to providing a quality service to internal and external customers and suppliers
Who are we?
TDX is a true New Zealand success story and 100% New Zealand owned and operated. From humble beginnings when we were set up over 40 years ago by a couple of mates, today TDX is recognised as the market leader for sales and service of construction equipment. We service our highly valued customers in the civil, forestry, construction, mining and marine sectors across all of New Zealand.

TDX is the distributor of leading global brands including Volvo CE, Yanmar CE, Shell Lubricants, Fuchs Kohler Generators, Perkins Engines and Allison Transmissions. We are committed to combining world-class experience with local know-how.

What’s in it for you?
  • Supportive and friendly team environment
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities
  • Weekly pay
  • company bonus
  • On-site parking
  • Discounts on retail products
  • Life insurance
  • Discounted medical insurance
  • Opportunities to grow your career with a market-leading New Zealand-owned business
At TDX, we are passionate about supporting our people and creating a workplace where everyone can succeed. You’ll be part of a team that works together, values each other’s contribution, and is committed to delivering the best possible customer experience every time.

You will ideally have:
  • Previous experience in a parts department or similar customer-focused role
  • Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills
  • The ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
  • Confidence using computer systems, including Microsoft Office
  • A positive and enthusiastic attitude with a willingness to learn
  • The ability to work both independently and as part of a team

If you’re looking for an opportunity to grow your career with a leading New Zealand-owned business and bring your passion for parts and customer service, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now and become part of the TDX team.

job.title: Recruiter - NZ Talent Solutions
job.description:
• Competitive salary + uncapped commission + evolving benefits program
  • Own and build a specialist trans-Tasman talent market
  • Strong career development opportunities within an established recruitment business
About Us:

Stellar Recruitment is a leading recruitment business with more than 20 years of experience supporting clients across mining, construction, infrastructure, industrial and professional markets.
With established operations across Australia and New Zealand and with continued growth across our key sectors. We are looking for an experienced Recruiter to join our Brisbane team and take ownership of an exciting new talent strategy focused on connecting skilled New Zealand-based candidates with opportunities across Australia.

The Opportunity:

This is not a traditional recruitment desk. You will take ownership of developing a scalable New Zealand to Australia talent pipeline, building long-term candidate communities across sectors experiencing ongoing skills shortages.
You will identify, engage and qualify talent while helping position New Zealand candidate markets as a genuine workforce solution for our clients.


Your Role:
You will be responsible for building and maintaining structured talent pools across areas including:
  • Mining, including mobile plant, maintenance and supervision
  • Construction and infrastructure, including project management, engineering, supervision and trades
  • Industrial and manufacturing trades
You will proactively identify candidates based on relocation readiness, Australian employment eligibility, salary expectations and alignment with current and future client demand.

You will also:
  • Build an engaged and continuously growing NZ candidate database
  • Develop ongoing candidate engagement campaigns rather than relying solely on job advertising
  • Plan and execute targeted sourcing campaigns across key New Zealand locations
  • Coordinate candidate events, information sessions and pre-qualified interview days
  • Partner with marketing on NZ-specific digital, social and email campaigns
  • Provide candidates with practical insights into Australian opportunities, salaries and relocation considerations
  • Work closely with Stellar's recruitment and BD teams to provide live candidate pipelines and market intelligence
  • Participate in selected client meetings to provide insight into candidate availability and workforce trends
  • Develop sector-specific NZ talent solutions for clients experiencing labour shortages
What We're Looking For:

You will be an experienced recruiter who enjoys building markets, developing candidate relationships and identifying new commercial opportunities.
To be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • A minimum of 2 years' recruitment experience
  • Strong candidate sourcing and engagement capability
  • Confidence building relationships with clients and candidates
  • Commercial awareness and strong negotiation skills
  • Sound judgement, decision-making and problem-solving ability
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong planning, organisation and time management skills
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • High attention to detail
  • A proactive, self-motivated approach and willingness to take ownership
Why Join Stellar:

At Stellar, we back our people to build successful careers and take ownership of their markets.

You'll benefit from:
  • Uncapped commission and a competitive salary package
  • An evolving employee benefits program
  • Clear career development and progression opportunities
  • An established brand with more than 20 years of industry experience
  • A strong and stable client portfolio
  • Support from experienced recruitment, business development and marketing teams
  • Regular team events and initiatives
  • A collaborative, high-performance culture where success is recognised
Ready to Build Something?

If you are an experienced recruiter looking for an opportunity where you can genuinely build and own a specialist talent market, we'd love to hear from you.
